sentences: Dreamteam, an AI-native CRM startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to take on Salesforce and HubSpot.
The company will use the funding to extend its platform beyond sales into other stages of the customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding, customer success and upselling.
Traditional CRM software depends on sales teams typing in customer information and updating records by hand.

Dreamteam, an AI-native CRM, is trying to remove most of that work.
The premise is that an AI system should capture what happened in calls, emails and meetings.

Read More: Unsiloed AI Raises $7.5 Mn Led By Felicis To Make Documents Computable
That is a bigger change than it sounds.
A CRM is only as good as its data.
The data is usually stale because nobody enjoys updating it.
Dreamteam was founded in 2025 by Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy, all former senior executives at Freshworks.
Venkatraman, the chief executive, has spent more than 25 years in enterprise software, including stints at Salesforce and Freshworks.
Kanthaswamy spent over nine years at Freshworks and most recently led product at Freshservice.
Parthasarathy worked on AI and platform engineering.
All three Dreamteam founders were part of Freshworks’ journey from an early-stage startup to a publicly listed company.
Is the relevant experience for building a challenger to incumbents.
Dreamteam is based in San Francisco with more than 35 employees.
Its engineering team sits in Chennai, while go-to-market operations run from the United States.
That split at Dreamteam is deliberate.
Engineering in India keeps the cost base competitive.
A US sales presence is still necessary to sell enterprise software to American buyers.
Together Fund, co-founded by Freshworks co-founder Girish Mathrubootham, was the first institutional investor in the company.
For Dreamteam, CRM is one of the largest categories in enterprise software.
It has been dominated by the same platforms for two decades.
Those products were built for a world where a salesperson entered data after a meeting.
Agents and automated capture change that assumption, which opens room for a system designed around it.
Salesforce and HubSpot have enormous distribution, large partner ecosystems and the ability to add AI features to existing contracts at little extra cost.
AI-native CRM has become a crowded pitch.
Several startups claiming they can replace Salesforce rather than sit beside it.
The differentiator for Dreamteam is the team’s operating history.
Building Freshworks from startup to listing is a specific skill set that most founders in this category do not have.
The Freshworks connection also opens doors with investors.
Together Fund’s early cheque is a signal of confidence rather than a coincidence.
Dreamteam will also be judged on how quickly it ships beyond sales, since the pitch promises the whole customer lifecycle rather than one module.
Its Chennai engineering base gives it a cost advantage over San Francisco rivals, and that advantage compounds as the product matures.
Three things will decide whether Dreamteam becomes a company or a feature.
The first is whether the AI capture is accurate enough that sales teams trust the record without checking it.
Winning a customer from an incumbent means migrating years of pipeline history.
That migration is where most challengers stall.
If the product charges per seat while reducing the number of seats a company needs, buyers will notice the contradiction.
